chapters.title: Chapter 5: Claiming Your TDS Credit and Refund

lessons.title: Claiming TDS in Your ITR and Getting Your Refund

body.text: A refund is simply the TDS you have already paid minus the tax you actually owe. Nobody sends it to you automatically. You claim it by filing an accurate return on time, verifying it, and giving the department a bank account it can pay into.

children.text: Ritu, 27, a data analyst in Pune, earns a salary of ₹9,00,000, has ₹60,000 of FD interest and did freelance dashboard work worth ₹1,50,000 for a Mumbai company. Her employer deducted nothing, correctly, because her salary alone was within the rebate. But her bank deducted ₹6,000 and her client ₹15,000. Her total tax for tax year 2026-27 is nil. The ₹21,000 will only come back if she files a return. This lesson shows how she claims it and what happens after she clicks submit.
The Filing Calendar for Tax Year 2026-27

body.text: Filing after the due date attracts a late fee of up to ₹5,000, or up to ₹1,000 if total income is ₹5,00,000 or less (formerly Section 234F). Even when you are due a refund and owe no tax, a late return costs you some refund interest, and in some cases benefits such as carrying forward certain losses.

children.text: Where TDS Goes in Your Return

Every return form has schedules where you list tax already paid, and the portal pre-fills most of it from your tax credit statement. Your job is to check the pre-filled figures, not accept them blindly.

body.caption: Tax already paid, as it appears in a return

cells: Every employer's TAN and TDS matches your statement
TDS on other income such as interest, fees, rent and dividends
Income is reported under the right head and in the right year
TDS deducted by buyers or tenants through Form 141
The buyer's or tenant's PAN and amount are correct

markDefs.definition: TDS shown in an earlier year's statement on income that is taxable in a later year. The return lets you carry it forward and claim it in the year the income is reported.

children.text: One rule governs every TDS line: credit is given in the year in which the related income is taxable. If TDS is deducted in one year on income you will report in a later year, you can carry it forward as
and claim it then. What you cannot do is claim TDS on income you are not reporting.

body.title: Quick Check: TDS Without the Income
body.question: Ritu's client deducted ₹15,000 on ₹1,50,000 of fees. She decides the work was "just a side gig" and leaves the fees out of her return, but claims the ₹15,000 TDS to boost her refund. What is likely to happen?
options: Her refund is processed in full, since the TDS is in her statement
The TDS credit or the income mismatch will be flagged, and she may face a demand or notice
The client is penalised instead of Ritu
Nothing, because side income below ₹5 lakh need not be reported
body.explanation: TDS credit is linked to the income it was deducted on. Claiming the credit while omitting the income is exactly the kind of mismatch automated processing picks up, and the client has already reported the payment against her PAN. The correct approach is to report the fees, using presumptive taxation if eligible, and then claim the TDS.

body.title: Try It: Ritu's Refund
body.prompt: Ritu's total tax is ₹0 after the rebate. Her bank deducted ₹6,000 and her client ₹15,000. Her employer deducted nothing and she paid no advance tax. What refund is due?
body.explanation: Taxes already paid total ₹21,000. Final tax is nil, so the entire ₹21,000 is refundable. Because she has professional income and uses presumptive taxation, she files ITR-4, due by 31 August 2027.

events.title: Return filed
events.description: Ritu files ITR-4 on the e-filing portal, with income and TDS matching her statement.

events.title: E-verified
events.description: She verifies instantly using an Aadhaar OTP. Without verification within 30 days, the return would be treated as not filed.

events.title: Processing
events.description: The Centralised Processing Centre checks the return and computes tax, interest and refund under Section 270 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (formerly Section 143(1)).

events.title: Intimation
events.description: She receives an intimation by email showing the department's computation and the refund determined.

events.title: Refund credited
events.description: The refund, with any interest due, is credited to her pre-validated bank account.

markDefs.definition: Interest at 0.5% per month or part of a month on a tax refund, formerly under Section 244A. For a return filed on time, it generally runs from 1 April after the tax year ends until the refund is granted. For a late return, it starts from the date of filing.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: Verification
body.textWithBlank: After filing, you must verify your return within ___ days, or it is treated as if it was never filed.
body.explanation: You can e-verify instantly using an Aadhaar OTP, net banking, or a bank or demat account EVC. Posting a signed ITR-V is also allowed. Refunds are not processed until the return is verified.

body.text: Refunds are paid only to a bank account that is pre-validated on the e-filing portal in your name and linked to your PAN. A closed account, a name mismatch with PAN, or an inoperative PAN are the most common reasons refunds fail. Check the Refund/Demand Status on the portal if nothing arrives after processing, and request a refund reissue once the problem is fixed.

children.text: When Your Refund Is Adjusted Against an Old Demand

If the department thinks you owe tax for an earlier year, it can set your refund off against that demand. Before doing so it sends an intimation (formerly under Section 245) and gives you an opportunity to respond, typically within 30 days.

body.title: Scenario: The Surprise Demand
body.scenario: Soon after filing, Ritu receives an intimation proposing to adjust ₹8,000 of her ₹21,000 refund against an outstanding demand for an earlier year. She checks and finds the demand arose because an earlier employer's TDS never appeared in her statement that year, although it was deducted from her salary.
body.modelAnswer: She should not ignore the intimation. On the e-filing portal, under the response to outstanding demand, she should select that she disagrees with the demand, give the reason (TDS deducted but not credited), and upload proof such as that year's Form 16 and payslips. At the same time she should ask the earlier employer to file a correction statement for that year so the credit appears, and then request rectification of the old intimation so the demand is reduced or cancelled. If she responds in time, the department should not adjust the disputed amount without considering her reply. If she ignores it, ₹8,000 will simply be taken from her refund, and she would then have to fight to get it back.

body.title: Claim Every Rupee of TDS
steps: Reconcile your tax credit statement with your records, as covered in Lesson 1
Report all income that TDS was deducted on, under the right head and in the right year
Check every pre-filled TDS line against your certificates before submitting
Pre-validate a bank account in your name on the e-filing portal
File before the due date and e-verify the same day
Track the intimation and refund status, and respond within the time allowed to any proposed adjustment

body.label: Income Tax e-Filing Portal
body.description: File and e-verify your return, pre-validate a bank account, check Refund/Demand Status and respond to outstanding demand intimations.

cards.definition: TDS, TCS, advance tax and self-assessment tax paid, minus final tax for the year, when the result is positive.
Processing of returns and issue of intimations under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Formerly Section 143(1).
0.5% per month or part of a month, from 1 April after the tax year if filed on time, or from the date of a late filing. Formerly Section 244A.
TDS from an earlier year carried forward and claimed in the year the related income is taxable.
A bank account verified on the e-filing portal in your name. Refunds are paid only into such accounts.
Setting a refund off against an outstanding demand for another year, after an intimation you can respond to. Formerly Section 245.

points: Refunds of excess TDS come only through a filed and verified return, never automatically
For tax year 2026-27, most individuals file by 31 July 2027, those with non-audit business or professional income by 31 August 2027, and revised returns are allowed until 31 March 2028
Claim TDS in the year the related income is taxable, and always report the income you claim TDS on
Check pre-filled TDS lines against your certificates, and pre-validate a bank account in your own name
Refunds on time carry interest at 0.5% a month from 1 April after the tax year, while late returns earn less and attract a late fee
Respond promptly to any intimation proposing to adjust your refund against an old demand, with proof if you disagree
